title: Extreme Power Mean Limits: M_r → max and min
description: Proves the two extreme power mean limits: lim_{r→+∞} M_r(x) = max(x) and lim_{r→-∞} M_r(x) = min(x). The max case uses a squeeze between M·n^{-1/r} and M, with n^{-1/r} → 1. The min case reduces to the max case via the duality identity M_r(x) = (M_{-r}(1/x))⁻¹. 2 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

meta.author: Lean Genius
originalContributions: powerMean_tendsto_max: M_r(x) → max(x) as r → +∞, proved by squeezing between max·n^{-1/r} and max
powerMean_tendsto_min: M_r(x) → min(x) as r → -∞, proved by duality with the max case via M_r(x) = (M_{-r}(1/x))⁻¹

overview.historicalContext: The power mean M_r(x) = (Σ xᵢ^r / n)^{1/r} was studied systematically by Andrey Kolmogorov (1930) and independently by Mark Nagumo (1930), who characterized the class of quasi-arithmetic means. The extreme limits — M_r → max as r → +∞ and M_r → min as r → -∞ — appear as Theorem 4 in Hardy, Littlewood, and Pólya's 'Inequalities' (1934, Cambridge University Press), where they note these limits complete the interpolation picture: min = M_{-∞} ≤ ⋯ ≤ HM = M_{-1} ≤ GM = M_0 ≤ AM = M_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ max = M_{+∞}. The intuition is that raising to a large positive power r amplifies the largest component exponentially relative to smaller ones, so the r-th root of the average converges to the maximum. The squeeze argument used here — bounding between M·n^{-1/r} and M, with n^{-1/r} → 1 — is essentially the approach in HLP §2.9. The duality identity M_r(x) = (M_{-r}(1/x))⁻¹, used for the min case, reflects the order-reversing nature of inversion on positive reals and was already implicit in Schur's 1923 work on convex functions.
overview.problemStatement: For x : ι → ℝ with all xᵢ > 0, prove: (1) M_r(x) → max(x) as r → +∞; (2) M_r(x) → min(x) as r → -∞.
overview.text: The max case (powerMean_tendsto_max) uses a squeeze: for r > 0, M * n^{-1/r} ≤ M_r(x) ≤ M where M = max(x). The upper bound holds because each xᵢ^r ≤ M^r. The lower bound uses the single-element contribution from the maximizer. Since n^{-1/r} → 1 as r → +∞, both bounds converge to M. The min case (powerMean_tendsto_min) sets g = 1/x, observes sup'(g) = (inf'(x))⁻¹, applies the max case to g, then inverts using M_r(x) = (M_{-r}(g))⁻¹ and the filter composition atBot → atTop via negation.
overview.proofStrategy: Max case: tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le' with lower bound M*n^{-1/r} (via sup_mul_pow_le_powerMean) and constant upper bound M (via powerMean_le_sup). Min case: duality M_r(x) = (M_{-r}(g))⁻¹ for r ≠ 0 (eventually near atBot), composed with Filter.tendsto_neg_atBot_atTop.
keyInsights: c^{-1/r} → 1 as r → +∞: proved as tendsto_const_rpow_neg_inv_atTop via -r⁻¹ → 0 and continuity of c^·
Squeeze between M*n^{-1/r} and M gives the max limit; the factor n^{-1/r} accounts for the count of terms in the mean
Duality identity: (xᵢ⁻¹)^{-r} = ((xᵢ)^r)⁻¹)⁻¹ = xᵢ^r via Real.inv_rpow + Real.rpow_neg + inv_inv
Filter composition: atBot →(negation)→ atTop converts the min limit to the max limit of the inverted function
Antitone inversion: sup'(1/x) = 1/inf'(x) — taking reciprocals reverses the order for positive values
prerequisites: tendsto_const_rpow_neg_inv_atTop: c^{-1/r} → 1 as r → +∞ (proved in this file)
Real.inv_rpow, Real.rpow_neg: algebraic identities for inverse and negation in rpow
Filter.tendsto_neg_atBot_atTop: the negation map sends atBot to atTop

conclusion.summary: Both extreme power mean limits proved: max at +∞ and min at -∞. 2 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms, 220 lines.
conclusion.implications: Completes the extreme cases of power mean theory. Together with the monotonicity results (OQ-03-OQ-02-OQ-01 through OQ-03), this establishes the full interpolation picture: M_{-∞} = min ≤ M_r ≤ max = M_{+∞}. The squeeze argument and duality identity are reusable techniques for other mean limit problems.
openQuestions: Prove the weighted power mean limits: lim_{r→±∞} M_r(x, w) = max/min(x) for any positive weight vector w with Σwᵢ = 1
Formalize the full Pythagorean means interpolation: HM ≤ GM ≤ AM as special cases of the power mean monotonicity chain

sections.title: Module Header and Imports
sections.summary: Docstring documenting the extreme power mean limits and proof strategy, Mathlib import, namespace/open declarations, and universe variables for the finite nonempty index type ι.

sections.title: Power Mean Definition
sections.summary: Defines the unweighted power mean M_r(x) as a piecewise function: (Σ xᵢ^r / n)^{1/r} for r ≠ 0, and (∏ xᵢ)^{1/n} for r = 0 (geometric mean).

sections.title: Key Limit: c^{-1/r} → 1
sections.summary: tendsto_const_rpow_neg_inv_atTop: for any c > 0, c^{-1/r} → 1 as r → +∞, proved via -r⁻¹ → 0 and continuity of c^(·) at 0.

sections.title: Squeeze Bounds for Max Case
sections.summary: Auxiliary card_pos lemma, then the two bound lemmas: powerMean_le_sup (upper bound: M_r ≤ max, via each xᵢ^r ≤ M^r) and sup_mul_pow_le_powerMean (lower bound: max·n^{-1/r} ≤ M_r, via single-term contribution from the maximizer).

sections.title: Max Limit Theorem
sections.summary: powerMean_tendsto_max: M_r → max(x) as r → +∞ via tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le' (squeeze) between the two bounds, with filter_upwards restricting to r > 0.

sections.title: Min Limit Theorem
sections.summary: powerMean_tendsto_min: M_r → min(x) as r → -∞. Constructs g = 1/x, proves sup'(g) = (inf'(x))⁻¹ via le_antisymm (antitone inversion), applies the max theorem to g, inverts via Tendsto.inv₀, establishes the duality identity M_r(x) = (M_{-r}(g))⁻¹, and composes with Filter.tendsto_neg_atBot_atTop.

references.text: Hardy, G. H., Littlewood, J. E. & Pólya, G. (1952). Inequalities, 2nd ed. Cambridge University Press.
Steele, J. M. (2004). The Cauchy-Schwarz Master Class. Cambridge University Press.
